passage: Minakshi, eighteen months, clung to Paati's sari as the new neighbour smiled down at her. "Hello, little one!" The neighbour reached out. Minakshi hid her face and whimpered. Bhavna Chithi came in from the kitchen. "Minu! Come to me!" Minakshi's arms shot up. On Chithi's hip she quietened, but still watched the stranger warily. "Sing the rain song," Paati said. Bhavna Chithi hummed the lullaby Amma sang every night. Minakshi's head sank onto her shoulder. Her thumb went to her mouth.

qa.q: What did Minakshi cling to when the neighbour smiled?
qa.a: Paati's sari.

qa.q: What does Minakshi's head sinking onto Chithi's shoulder suggest?
qa.a: Minakshi feels calm and safe with a known face and the lullaby she hears every night.

qa.q: What helped Minakshi settle, and how could the family handle the next visit from a stranger?
qa.a: A familiar person and Amma's lullaby helped; next time the family could keep Minakshi on a known lap and let the visitor warm up slowly.

qa.q: How might the new neighbour feel when Minakshi hides?
qa.a: The neighbour may feel a little disappointed but likely understands; with more visits the neighbour may become familiar too.

grounding: A toddler hides from a new neighbour but calms with a familiar aunt and a known lullaby.

passage: Crèche note, Monday. Salma, caregiver. Kiran (2) cried hard at drop-off; a relief helper he had never seen was on this morning. He turned away whenever she reached for him. When I came in at nine, he crawled onto my lap and quietened. I played the counting song his mother sings at home, and he swayed along, calm. After snack he let the new helper sit near him, but not hold him. Plan: she joins our song time for a few days before trying again.

qa.q: Who was on duty that morning whom Kiran had never seen?
qa.a: A relief helper.

qa.q: What does Kiran turning away from the helper suggest?
qa.a: Kiran felt unsure and unsafe with an unfamiliar face and wanted someone known.

qa.q: Why is the plan for the new helper to join song time a good choice?
qa.a: Sitting in with the familiar song lets Kiran see the helper again and again, so the helper becomes familiar before trying to hold him.

qa.q: How might the relief helper feel on being turned away?
qa.a: The helper might feel a bit rejected, but it isn't personal; the helper is simply new to Kiran.

grounding: A crèche note shows a toddler wary of a new helper but calmed by a known caregiver and a familiar song.

passage: At the temple fair in Hosur, the crowd pressed close, and a man in a painted tiger mask bent down to wave. Vinita, two, screamed and buried her face in Amma's neck. A lady offered her a sugar sweet; she batted it away. Her big brother Tejas pushed through with two balloons. "Vinu! It's me!" She peeked, then reached for his finger. Tejas began humming the bhajan Dadi sang every evening. Vinita's sobs slowed. She rested her cheek on Amma's shoulder, holding Tejas's finger tight, watching the tiger man.

qa.q: What did Vinita do when a lady offered her a sugar sweet?
qa.a: She batted it away.

qa.q: What was Vinita feeling when she screamed at the tiger mask?
qa.a: Vinita was frightened by the strange, pressing crowd and an unfamiliar masked face.

qa.q: What did Tejas do that helped, and what could the family try at the next fair?
qa.a: Tejas offered a known face and hummed Dadi's evening bhajan; next time the family could keep Vinita close and hum familiar songs through the busy parts.

qa.q: How might the lady with the sweet see Vinita's reaction?
qa.a: The lady probably meant kindness and may feel brushed off, but could understand that a small child is wary of strangers.

grounding: A toddler at a crowded fair is frightened by strangers but calms with her brother and a familiar family song.

passage: Grandma's birthday in Oslo: the living room was full of tall, loud guests. Selin, two, stood by the sofa, thumb in mouth. A lady she had never seen bent down, smiling. "Hei!" Selin's lip wobbled and she ducked behind the curtain. Then her uncle Lars, who came every Sunday, crouched there and began the boat song he always sang. Selin peeked out, climbed onto his knee and swayed with him, one eye still on the lady.

qa.q: Where did Selin hide when the lady bent down?
qa.a: She ducked behind the curtain.

qa.q: What does Selin keeping one eye on the lady suggest about how she felt?
qa.a: Even calmed by Lars and his song, she still seemed wary of the unfamiliar face.

qa.q: How could the family help Selin feel safer at the next party?
qa.a: They could keep a familiar person like Lars nearby and let new guests say hello slowly from a little distance.

qa.q: How might the lady feel when Selin hides from her?
qa.a: She might feel a little disappointed, but probably understands that small children are shy with strangers.

grounding: A toddler is wary of a stranger and calmed by a familiar uncle and the song he always sings.

passage: I'm Shalini from next door. On Saturday I minded Lalremsiami for an hour while her mother ran to the pharmacy. Siami is eighteen months old. When the door shut, she wailed. I made faces, offered biscuits, sang a rhyme. She pushed my hands away. Then I played her grandmother's nightly voice note, the same slow Mizo lullaby. Siami went quiet mid-sob, hugged her cloth rabbit and stared at the phone. I can't say what she felt, but she stayed calm till her mother came back.

qa.q: How old is Siami?
qa.a: She is eighteen months old.

qa.q: Why might Siami have gone quiet when she heard the lullaby?
qa.a: Her grandmother's familiar voice and song seemed to make her feel safe, even with a neighbour she didn't know well.

qa.q: What could Siami's mother leave with a neighbour next time?
qa.a: She could leave the lullaby recording and Siami's cloth rabbit, familiar things that help her settle.

qa.q: How might Siami's mother feel on hearing about the lullaby?
qa.a: She might feel relieved and touched that her mother's nightly voice note comforted Siami while she was away.

grounding: A neighbour observes a toddler reject an unfamiliar sitter but calm to her grandmother's familiar lullaby.
